$comment: The ProseMirror schema for a Memberberry note. This file is the cross-language
contract required by SPEC.md §5.6: the Tiptap schema (M3, TypeScript) is generated
from it, and the `yrs` walker (M2, Rust) is validated against it by
crates/mb-core/tests/schema.rs. Editing one side without the other is a test failure,
Every node here has exactly one canonical Markdown rendering (SPEC.md §4.4), because
under C2 the schema *is* the contract with the file format. A node that cannot be
written as Markdown does not belong in this file.
Frontmatter is deliberately absent. It is a map of scalars and string lists, not
prose, so it lives in the sibling `frontmatter` Y.Map rather than this ProseMirror
document (A25). That gives each key independent merge semantics.
Attribute types use a small vocabulary understood by both generators:
string | boolean | integer | enum | date | string[] | enum[]
`optional: true` means the attribute's default is null.

doc.$comment: A note with no blocks is `doc(paragraph)`; canonicalization drops the empty paragraph, so it serializes to an empty file.

heading.$comment: Setext headings parse but never serialize; ATX is the canonical form.

ordered_list.markdown: 1. (lazy numbering — every item writes the start value or `1.`, the renderer counts)
ordered_list.$comment: Orderedness is a property of the list, not the item: `1. [ ] x` is a task in an ordered list, so task_item appears under both list types.

list_item.$comment: Not in the block group: a list item is only ever a child of a list. `block*`, not `block+`: a bare `- ` line parses to an item with no content, so the model must hold one.

task_item.$comment: `unknown` holds metadata markers this version does not model — recurrence (🔁) above all — verbatim and in source order. Dropping it would destroy user data on the first edit, so generators must round-trip it untouched, never normalize it.

blockquote.$comment: `block*`, not `block+`: a bare `>` line is valid Markdown and parses to an empty blockquote, so the model must be able to hold one.

callout.$comment: `kind` is a free string, not an enum: Obsidian accepts any identifier and unknown kinds must round-trip rather than be coerced to `note`.

callout_title.$comment: A node rather than an attribute because the title is inline content — it can hold links, emoji and emphasis, which an attribute cannot represent.

code_block.markdown: backtick fence, minimum 3, extended to exceed any inner run

divider.$comment: `***` rather than `---`, which would be ambiguous with a frontmatter fence at the top of a file.

table.$comment: The first table_row is the header; GFM has no headerless table, and `table_row+` is what makes its presence structural. `alignments` is per column and its length is the column count.

soft_break.markdown: a single newline inside a paragraph
soft_break.$comment: A node rather than a newline inside a text node so that the soft/hard distinction survives a round trip; ProseMirror text nodes conventionally hold no newlines.

hard_break.markdown: a backslash at end of line

wikilink.$comment: `anchor_kind`/`anchor_text` flatten the Rust `Option<Anchor>` enum, which ProseMirror attributes cannot hold directly. `anchor_kind: none` requires `anchor_text: null` and vice versa — enforced by the validator, not the schema.

emoji.$comment: Custom emoji only. Unicode emoji are stored as their literal glyph in a text node, because a glyph still renders in a plain text editor (SPEC.md §11.3).

em.$comment: `*` is canonical; `_` is emitted only where `*` would not reparse (see serialize::emphasis_delimiter).

code.$comment: Excludes every other mark: a code span's content is literal, so emphasis inside it has no Markdown rendering.
